problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -11 & 4 & 6 \\ 7 & 7 & -3 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{3}$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?

examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071806/assets/81176c8bb51128cdaf5d72842e2b2b909b1c41d63249eb3640d745bc9e0c7f9b.png)

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- $C_1:=\ldots$

- $C_3:= C_3 - 4C_2$

- $C_4:= \ldots$

each of the form $C_i:=C_i+kC_2,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
examples.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of $a_{32}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -1 & -6 \\ 7 & -2 & -2 & -4 \\ -5 & 1 & 4 & 2 \\ -8 & -3 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+5{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -3 & -1 & -6 \\ -3 & -2 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 2 \\ -23 & -3 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-4{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -3 & 11 & -6 \\ -3 & -2 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -23 & -3 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -3 & 11 & 0 \\ -3 & -2 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -23 & -3 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\qquad$ $C_1:=C_1+5C_2\quad$ and $\quad C_4:=C_4-2C_2.$

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 & -16 \\ -2 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}9 & 7 & 20 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
feedback.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 & -16 \\ -2 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 7 & -16 \\ -2 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 7 & 20 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+{C}_{1}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{1}.$
